commit.message:
Keep the ring across a descent, and name DSC-4 when it is wrong

Work package 8 of milestone 0.7, the first of the corrections the audit
of 0.7.0rc1 asked for. Both findings reproduce exactly as reported.

The target was rebuilt with the expression constructor, which re-infers
a ring. A source over QQ gave a target over ZZ; over a finite field that
changes the characteristic and with it the arithmetic of every step
after this one, and step.ring was not equal to target.ring although the
property promises the target's context. It is built with clone_ring and
reindex now, which is the idiom peeling.undo already uses to drop a
coordinate. reindex is sound exactly when the deleted generator has
exponent zero in every surviving term, which is the second half of
DSC-3, so the check that stood there for another reason is what licenses
the call.

The ring property called PolyRing.clone, which goes through SymPy's
cache and handed the same mutable object back on every access, so a
caller could reach a step's generators through it. That is precisely
what clone_ring exists to prevent, and its docstring records the failure
-- a shared domain that converted T*u to zero. The property uses it now.
The mistake is worth naming rather than quietly fixing: this milestone
wrote a roadmap paragraph about that cache and then called past it.

DSC-4 asked for automorphisms over the source's ring and nothing
checked. A wrong ring surfaced from inside
ElementaryAutomorphism.apply_to as a bare ValueError naming neither the
obligation nor the side it came from. _verify_changes runs first in
verify and is also called from the derived parts, so a caller who
reaches for the conjugate or the target first gets the same named
exception rather than the bare one.

DSC-2 gains the domain and the order, and DSC-4 the sentence that being
over the source's ring is checked. Neither is a new obligation; both say
what the family already meant and what the code did not do.

Six tests: the domain and order over QQ, GF(5) and a grlex ring, the
ring being a fresh object on every access, the two sides of the DSC-4
message, and the derived parts refusing a foreign automorphism.

No figure moves. This package changes what a step produces over rings
other than the default and what it says when it refuses, and nothing
about which chains exist. The carrier selector the audit reported
separately is WP 10 and does move figures, which is why it is not here.

commit.message:
Prepare 0.7.0rc1

The version moves to 0.7.0rc1 in the four places that have to agree:
pyproject.toml, the project status of the README, the topmost heading of
the changelog and CITATION.cff.

The ten [0.7] markers are gone from docs/contracts.md, which moving the
declared version forces: the marker test compares against the release
part of the version, so 0.7.0rc1 makes every [0.7] on the page fail.
HOM-11, HOM-12, UNT-12 and DSC-1 to DSC-7 are now plain obligations. The
page gains the milestone paragraph, in the shape the 0.6 one has, and
names the two of the ten a reviewer should weigh differently: DSC-3, the
only obligation whose failure says nothing about the map it was given,
and HOM-12, the only one whose hypothesis is a property the source is
not required to have.

The DOI does not move and the README no longer says it does. It said the
number was the DOI of this version, which was true while the version was
0.6.0. A release candidate is not deposited and has no DOI of its own,
so both files say plainly that 10.5281/zenodo.22299353 belongs to 0.6.0
and stands beside a version that has moved past it. The test that holds
the two copies together compares the two DOIs and neither against a
version, so it stayed green through the false sentence; that is worth
knowing rather than fixing here.

The README's milestone section is rewritten for 0.7 and its "next" for
0.8. Three claims elsewhere in it had gone stale with the descent: that
compression is the one step that lowers a dimension, that there are
seven step types, and the feature list having no entry for the descent
at all. The same sentence on the contract page said the family is not
implemented, which stopped being true with WP 5.1.

The changelog entry is one consolidated entry, as 0.6 has, and states
the two negatives the milestone ends on because they are the result and
not a shortfall: eleven variables are not reachable under the present
offer from any map of the published chain where the question has been
settled, and widening the offer does not make the question askable.

docs/roadmap.md gains "Where the milestone stands", which lists the
seven packages and what each answered, including WP 3 as withdrawn.

Gates run here: ruff format --check, ruff check, mypy src,
mypy --strict scripts, pytest --cov (1880 passed, 16 deselected, 100%),
make reconstruct (16 of 16), make measure (every figure agrees). Left to
the maintainer and named as such: pytest -m "", scripts/mutation_probe.py
and make release with its lock-check, coverage, build-test, sdist-test,
dist-check and test-minimum. sdist-test is the one to watch: an audit of
0.6.0rc1 found a test failing there that had been failing since 0.5, and
this milestone added two test modules.

commit.message:
Write out what rewriting to degree three means, and take back a claim

Documentation only. The previous commit said that no BCWStep buys a
coordinate carrying a sum, and concluded that the published
eleven-variable map is not the output of a chain. Both are wrong.

A Fresh slot takes an arbitrary polynomial. That is why UNT-6 exists at
all, offering a divisor against a sum of cofactors, and a step whose
bought coordinate carries -x^2 + x z_2 z_3 builds and verifies. The
claim was made from the shape of the published components rather than
from the type of a slot, and one call would have settled it.

The conclusion was wrong too, and the worked example the maintainer
asked for is what shows it. Alpoege's third component is
2x - 3x^2 z_2 - x^3 z_3. One BCWStep with both slots fresh, buying
coordinates for -x^2 and for x z_3, turns it into
-h k - h x z_3 + k x^2 - 3 x^2 z_2 + 2 x with h - x^2 and k + x z_3
beside it: one monomial of degree four becomes three of degree at most
three, which on the section h = x^2, k = -x z_3 sum back to -x^3 z_3.
That result is term for term the third component of
examples.spacerat11, and its ninth and tenth are the two bought ones. So
that component of the published map is one step of Proposition (3.1),
and the six steps peel found are a chain and not an artefact.

What survives is narrower and is what the package now says. The two
presentations differ in whether the abbreviations are chosen one at a
time, each against the residue the last one left, or all at once against
the original map. The published construction does the second and uses
eight. A search that does the first has to guess, at every map, which
abbreviation the ones after it will want. Whether the second formulation
is worth building is what WP 7 should measure before it widens anything.

docs/errata.md records it. The near miss is worth keeping: the claim was
about a shape the library does support.
